_allowedhosts_comment: Framework key, consumed by HostFilteringMiddleware, which the host inserts at position 0 of the pipeline - ahead of everything, /health and /ready included. Left as the wildcard here ON PURPOSE and set per environment; unlike the other shipped defaults this key has no safe non-wildcard value in a committed file. Never ship a curly-brace placeholder in it: an unreplaced one is not a warning, it is 400 Invalid Hostname on EVERY request and every probe, and the one line that explains it is logged at Information, which the Serilog Microsoft override below drops. Never use an empty string either: an empty value falls back to the wildcard, so it reads as tightened while allowing every host. Behind the API Gateway the correct value is the host of the YARP destination (AUTH_API_INTERNAL_URL), NOT your public domain: no RequestHeaderOriginalHost transform is configured, so the Host header arriving here is the destination's, and X-Forwarded-Host never reaches this filter (UseForwardedHeaders takes XForwardedFor and XForwardedProto only, and runs long after host filtering). The real perimeter for this application is the IIS hostname binding plus the firewall rule restricting this host to the Gateway.

ConnectionStrings._comment: Development: Uses Windows Auth. Production: Use appsettings.Production.json with SQL Auth + Encrypt=True

Jwt._comment: Keys are auto-generated on first startup via DPAPI. Override Issuer/Audience for production.

DataProtection._comment: KeyPath: where the Data Protection key ring is stored. Empty = default %ProgramData%\AuthSystem\Keys. On IIS / shared hosting the app-pool identity often cannot write under %ProgramData%, so set this to a writable folder OUTSIDE the public web root (the SAME folder the API Gateway uses, so both share one ring).

Certificate._comment: Only used when SecretManagement:StorageMode = Certificate. Prefer PasswordEnvironmentVariable over storing Password here.

SecretManagement._comment: StorageMode: PlainText | Certificate (default) | Dpapi. Certificate needs DataProtection:Certificate below; in Development ONLY, a missing certificate falls back to PlainText so a fresh clone runs without setup — every other environment fails to start instead. Keys auto-generate on first startup; disable AutoGenerateKeys after initial setup in production.
SecretManagement._PlainTextTargetFile_comment: Where PlainText-mode secrets are written. Empty = the running environment's own appsettings.{Environment}.json, which is what you want; set a path only to override.
SecretManagement._enableadminapi_comment: Ships FALSE so a deployment that never mentions this key is closed rather than open. It used to ship true, contradicting the class default in SecretManagementSettings.cs and the registry default in SystemSettingsRegistry.cs, which meant the /api/v1/admin/secrets/* endpoints ran live on any deployment that forgot to override it. Turn it on deliberately for the minutes you are provisioning or rotating keys, then turn it off. The console CANNOT re-enable it - the field is ReadOnly in the settings registry - so this is a file or environment-variable edit plus a restart, by design.

HealthChecks._comment: ExposeErrorDetails: include failed-check exception messages in the /health and /ready JSON. /health and /ready are PUBLIC (exempt from gateway-token validation), so keep this false in production; enable briefly only to diagnose. Full errors are always in the server logs.

Password._pepper_comment: Server-side secret mixed into every hash (defense-in-depth vs DB-only breach). Only 'Enabled' is set here; CurrentKeyId/Keys are secret-managed (auto-provisioned on startup when enabled). WARNING: once enabled, the pepper must be backed up like the JWT keys - losing it locks out all users.
Password._breach_comment: Reject or warn on known-breached passwords via the free, keyless HIBP Pwned Passwords range API (k-anonymity). Mode: Enforce = reject; Warn = allow but return X-Password-Warning header. FailOpen = allow if HIBP is unreachable. Fully inert (no external call) when Enabled=false.

Gateway._comment: ExpectedToken is auto-generated and loaded from DPAPI secrets file on first startup

ImageStorage._comment: Filesystem provider; the DB stores a relative key and the API composes PublicBaseUrl+key at read time. Swap Provider for object storage later without code changes. PublicBaseUrl/PhysicalPath are overridden per environment.

PrivacyPolicyPublication._comment: Production overrides PhysicalPath with the persistent folder mapped to accounts-sandbox.sebakhi.com/privacy. It must stay outside every application deployment directory.

_notifications_comment: === NOTIFICATION DISPATCH (DB-managed templates; UseOutbox=true queues sends for the background dispatcher) ===
_geoip_comment: === APPROXIMATE SIGN-IN LOCATION === Reads a local MaxMind GeoLite2-City .mmdb; there is no web-service mode, so no third party is told who signs in from where. Off until DatabasePath points at a real file: the lookup fails open, so leaving it on without one would silently show no locations at all. The file needs a MaxMind account and its own refresh cadence, and on shared hosting must sit where the app pool can read it.
_accountdeletion_comment: === ACCOUNT DELETION (two-phase: 30-day recoverable grace, then staged irreversible destruction) === IdentifierHmacKeyPlain is NEVER set here: PlainText mode auto-generates it into the git-ignored local settings layer; Certificate/Dpapi mode provisions AccountDeletionIdentifierHmacKey in the encrypted secrets file. That key is PERMANENT (identifier reservations depend on it) - never rotate it. PolicyVersion format is YYYY.MM; bump it when the documented retention policy changes.

AccountDeletion._migration_comment: RunEncryptionMigration: enable for ONE deployment to re-encrypt TOTP secrets and phone numbers under per-user keys (idempotent; watch the logged report), then disable.

_dataretention_comment: === DATA RETENTION === How long rows that already fell out of use are kept before the daily sweep deletes them. These windows are NOT about validity - every row here is already dead. They are about how long the row stays USEFUL as evidence: a revoked refresh token is what turns a stolen token into a detected theft, and a consumed authorization code is what proves a replay. Floors are enforced in code, so a zero here cannot sweep live rows. RefreshTokenDays is floored at 90 because the dashboard reports revocations over a window up to 90 days.
_datacontroller_comment: === DATA CONTROLLER === Legal identity published in the privacy policy. Empty by default on purpose: a policy cannot be published until the required fields are filled (System Settings -> Data controller). HostingCountry is a bare country name; the Turkish and French sentences add their own preposition.

Email._comment: Configure SMTP for password reset and email verification. Set Enabled=true when ready.

_registration_comment: === WHO MAY CREATE AN ACCOUNT === All three switches are ON here because that is what every deployment did before they existed; a closed door must be an operator's decision, not a surprise on upgrade. They cover the three doors that bring an account into existence for somebody who is not signed in: the public sign-up endpoint, the first sign-in of a Google/Apple identity matching no account, and the redemption of an organization invitation. They are separate because closing one usually means preferring another - a deployment that shuts public sign-up commonly wants invitations instead, and 'no passwords, Google only' is a real policy alongside its opposite. Close all three and the rule is exactly 'no account unless an administrator creates it'. The invitation door once sat outside this section on the reasoning that somebody had already decided the person belongs; that reasoning failed while the somebody could be any signed-in user, which is now governed separately by Organizations:AllowSelfServiceCreation and by the invite response no longer handing the inviter the token.
_organizations_comment: === WHO MAY CREATE AN ORGANIZATION === Its own section rather than a third Registration switch, because creating an organization creates no account - it creates AUTHORITY. The creator becomes the owner, and the seeded owner role carries the whole org:* family, invitation included, so this setting decides how many people can reach the invitation surface at all. Open here because the endpoint has always been reachable by any signed-in user and the accounts app offers the button on its own organizations page; an upgrade must not remove a shipped capability. Closing it does not disturb organizations that already exist and does not stop a holder of organizations:manage, who passes as an administrator rather than as a self-service user.
_identityprovider_comment: === IDENTITY PROVIDER (authorization-code + PKCE, IdP session cookie) ===

IdentityProvider._comment: AccountsBaseUrl = public origin of the accounts SPA (authorize redirects unauthenticated users to its /login). PublicBaseUrl = this API's OWN public origin (e.g. https://auth.example.com) — REQUIRED behind a reverse proxy, since Request.Host is the internal destination; used to build the authorize returnTo and the discovery-document endpoints.

ExternalAuth._google_comment: Off until a real ClientId is in place. The placeholder below is a NON-EMPTY string, so the usable-provider filter in GetExternalProvidersQueryHandler passes on client id alone: with Enabled=true a fresh deployment advertises google, the SPA renders the button, and every sign-in through it fails Google audience validation. Turn it on from System Settings after setting a real client id - ExternalAuth is console-editable and read per request, so no restart is needed. The seeded ExternalAuthProviders row for google is a SEPARATE switch and is ANDed with this one.
ExternalAuth._apple_comment: Enable only after the Apple Developer prerequisites exist (Services ID, verified domain + return URLs, .p8 key). PrivateKeyPem is NEVER set here: provision AppleSigningKeyPem in the encrypted secrets file (Certificate/Dpapi) or the git-ignored local settings layer in Development. Also flip the seeded 'apple' row in ExternalAuthProviders to IsEnabled=1.
ExternalAuth._avatar_import_comment: Copies the provider's profile picture into this system's image storage on the first external sign-in of an account that has no picture yet. Needed because img-src names this origin only, so a remote provider URL would render as the initials fallback. Set Enabled=false where the server has no outbound HTTP.

Cors._comment: REQUIRED for production: Specify allowed origins. Empty array + non-dev environment = startup error

RateLimiting._comment: One entry per NAMED policy that endpoints actually opt into (see Program.cs). There is no general/default bucket by design.

GatewayRateLimiting._comment: The GATEWAY's limiter, not this process's. Kept here because the gateway cannot read the database: it pulls these over /api/v1/internal/gateway-settings, so the console can own them. Must stay equal to API_Gateway/appsettings.json's RateLimiting section (GatewayRateLimitingParityTests).
